SaidiOwn your AI workforce

A self-hosted orchestrator you chat with. It plans the work, delegates it to agents scoped to your repos, verifies the result against observable criteria, and hands you a branch — on your private knowledge, under your approval, on infrastructure you own.

Get Started
What is Saidi?
View on GitHub

Runs, not chat sessions

Every task becomes a durable Run with its own thread, its own branch, and one shared context across every agent that touches it. Close the tab, restart the server — the Run survives.

How Runs work

Plans with real acceptance criteria

PRIME freezes a checklist of tasks, each with observable criteria and mechanical checks. A task only reaches done when an independent gate says so — not when the agent claims it.

Plans & Tasks

Agents organised into departments

Project agents scoped to one repo, custom agents grouped into departments with a lead that routes work to its team. Each with its own persona, skills, MCP servers, and tool permissions.

Agents & Departments

Delegation you can audit

The boss holds a small toolbelt — delegate_to_project, run_agent, remember — and every delegation lands in the Run thread with its cost, its model, and its result.

Delegation

Memory that lives with you

Plain markdown files under memory/, scoped per user, per project, and per agent. Config lives in your repos; memory lives in Saidi and is never committed to a client repo.

Memory & Conventions

Reflexes — CRONs with an event trigger

A normalized event bus (run.finished, run.failed, run.needs_approval, webhooks) plus rules with boolean match trees, cooldowns, dedup keys, and approval gates.

Reflexes & Events

Saidi in one loop ​

You only ever talk to PRIME. It writes the plan, hands each task to the right agent, relays their questions back to you, and summarises the outcome — you never have to hold the whole graph in your head.

Before you start ​

Read the guardrails page first

Saidi writes to real repositories. Set the approval mode and the spend limit you are comfortable with before your first autonomous Run — see Approval & Spend Guardrails. Agents never merge and never force-push, but they do commit and push branches.
